Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 62 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) and Severe Tropical Storm EMONG
Issued at: 8:00 AM, 25 July 2025(Friday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Bulacan, Pampanga, Metro Manila, Cavite, Rizal, Laguna, Zambales, Bataan and Batangas.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Possible FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Nueva Ecija, Quezon and Tarlac which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 11:00 AM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.

‘HINDI NASOSOLYUSYUNAN 'YUNG FLOOD, LUMALALA PA'

Political analyst Ronald Llamas emphasized that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. should take "decisive moves" to address problems in his administration's flood-control projects.

“Kailangan niya ng indication na seryoso siya diyan. Makikita mo naman, hindi nasosolusyunan 'yung flood. Lumalala pa,” Llamas said during an exclusive interview with The Philippine STAR Editor-in-Chief Amy Pamintuan.

His remarks came in light of recent reports of widespread flooding in Luzon, especially in Metro Manila, due to heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat.” #TruthOnTheLine
